newsitem.title: UK: Wong report has little impact on palmoil in Europe.
newsitem.headline: Wong report has little impact on palmoil in Europe.

text.p: Latest Malaysian output, stocks and exports estimates from Ivan Wong had little impact on palm oil prices in Europe on Tuesday.
Malaysian private forecaster Wong estimated local palmoil output during September at 843,000 tonnes, four percent up from August and against his privous estimate of a six percent rise.
Wong put palm oil stocks at 905,000 tonnes against offical figures of 800,893 tonnes at end-August. Exports were put at 645,000 tonnes against 638,601 tonnes in August.

Traders in Europe said the report was neutral to friendly, but at midday palm oil prices were little changed from Monday's close with crude palm oil $2.50 up and refined palm oils unchanged to $7.50 higher.
Trading was limited to one dated Oct trade in RBD oil at $506 and Nov at $500.
Olein fetched $543.50 for Oct, $530, $531 and #532.50 for Nov and $530 a tonne fob Malaysian ports for Dec.
Oct stearin traded at $375 in a two way switch with Dec at $385.
Laurtic oils were mixed with coconut oil $2.50 up to $5 down and palmkernel oil unchanged to $5 lower.

Soft oils were higher following overnight gains in Chicago with soy oil one to 0.50 guilders up and rape oil one guilder higher in a so far tradeless market. --Jim Ballantyne, London Newsroom +44 171 542 8062
